html:
The Wari' are an Indigenous people of the forests of Rondônia in western Brazil, near the Bolivian border, along tributaries of the Mamoré and Madeira rivers. The map shows them in 1492. They are not the same as the Wari of the Peruvian Andes, whose name is spelled alike.

They speak a Chapakuran language and farmed maize in forest clearings, hunting and fishing besides. For centuries they stayed out of the reach of outsiders.

During the rubber boom of the late 1800s, and again as railway builders and rubber tappers pushed into their land, the Wari' were attacked and fought back. Government agents and missionaries made peaceful contact in the late 1950s and early 1960s, and epidemics that followed killed a large share of them. A few thousand Wari' now live on reserved lands near Guajará-Mirim.
